²⁶ Each cherub stood ten cubits tall. ²⁷ Solomon placed the cherubim inside the inner sanctuary, and they spread their wings so that one wing of the first cherub touched one wall while a wing of the second cherub touched the opposite wall — and their inner wings touched each other in the middle of the room. ²⁸ He overlaid the cherubim with gold. ²⁹ He carved the walls of the entire house with figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers — all the way around, inside and out. ³⁰ He covered the floors with gold, inside and out.

³¹ For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the lintel and doorposts were a fifth of the wall's width. ³² Both doors were olive wood, and he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them, then overlaid them with gold, hammering the gold onto the cherubim and the palm trees. ³³ He made the same for the doorposts of the main hall — olive wood, a quarter of the wall's width. ³⁴ The two doors themselves were of cypress wood, each door having two folding leaves. ³⁵ He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them and covered them with gold laid evenly over the carved work.

³⁶ He built the inner courtyard with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams. ³⁷ The foundation of the LORD's house had been laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv. ³⁸ In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — the eighth month — the house was finished in every detail, exactly as it had been designed. Solomon had spent seven years building it.

[Chapter 7] ¹ Solomon also built his own palace, which took him thirteen years to complete. ² He built the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon — a hundred cubits long, fifty wide, and thirty high — supported by four rows of cedar columns with cedar beams across the tops. ³ The ceiling above the beams rested on forty-five pillars, fifteen per row, and was covered with cedar. ⁴ There were three rows of windows facing each other in sets of three, ⁵ and all the doors and doorframes were square — again, windows facing windows in three tiers.

⁶ He built a colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty wide, with a covered porch in front supported by pillars and a canopy overhead. ⁷ He also built the throne room — the Hall of Justice, where he would hear cases — and he paneled it with cedar from floor to ceiling. ⁸ His own living quarters, behind the hall in the inner courtyard, were built the same way. He also built a palace for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married, just like this hall. ⁹ All these buildings, from foundation to roofline and from the outside to the great courtyard, were built of fine dressed stone cut to measure and sawed smooth on all sides. ¹⁰ The foundations were laid with great stones — slabs of eight and ten cubits.

¹¹ Above the foundation were more dressed stones cut to size, and cedar beams. ¹² The great outer courtyard had three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams all the way around, just like the inner courtyard of the LORD's house and the entrance hall of the palace. ¹³ King Solomon sent to Tyre and brought a man named Hiram. ¹⁴ He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a craftsman from Tyre who worked in bronze. Hiram was brilliant — a master of all kinds of bronze work — and he came to King Solomon and carried out all the bronze work assigned to him. ¹⁵ He cast two bronze pillars, each eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference.

¹⁶ He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each one five cubits tall. ¹⁷ He decorated the capitals with lattice netting and twisted chains — seven strands of chainwork for each capital. ¹⁸ He made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates running around each network to cover the capitals at the top, and he did the same for both capitals. ¹⁹ The capitals on top of the pillars in the porch were shaped like lilies, four cubits tall. ²⁰ Above the rounded part beside the network, pomegranates ran in rows all the way around — two hundred pomegranates encircling each capital.

²¹ He erected the pillars at the porch of the temple. The right pillar he named Jachin, and the left pillar he named Boaz. ²² The tops of both pillars were shaped like lilies. And so the work on the pillars was finished. ²³ He made the great bronze basin — the Sea — ten cubits across, perfectly round, five cubits deep, and thirty cubits in circumference. ²⁴ All around the rim, just below the brim, were two rows of gourds encircling it — ten gourds per cubit, cast as part of the basin. ²⁵ The Sea rested on twelve bronze oxen — three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east — with the Sea mounted on top of them and all their haunches turned inward.

²⁶ The basin was a handsbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like a cup — like the petals of a lily. It held two thousand baths. ²⁷ Hiram also made ten bronze stands, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits tall. ²⁸ The stands were built with side panels set in frames, ²⁹ and on those panels — between the rails — were carved lions, oxen, and cherubim. Above and below the lions and oxen were decorative wreaths of hammered work. ³⁰ Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles. At the four corners were supports cast as part of the stand, and the supports beneath the basin were also cast with decorative wreaths at each side.

³¹ The opening at the top of each stand — inside the capital — was a cubit deep. The opening itself was round, a cubit and a half across, and around its edges were carvings and panels — square, not round. ³² Below the opening were four wheels fitted with bronze axles connected to the body of the stand. Each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter. ³³ The wheels were crafted like chariot wheels — their axles, hubs, spokes, and rims all cast in bronze. ³⁴ Each of the four corners had a cast support that was part of the stand itself. ³⁵ At the top of each stand was a round collar half a cubit high, and the panels and frames at the top were cast as part of the stand.

³⁶ On the surfaces of the panels and frames he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, with decorative borders all around. ³⁷ This is how he made all ten stands — all poured from the same mold, the same size, the same design. ³⁸ He also made ten bronze basins, one for each stand. Each basin was four cubits across and held forty baths. ³⁹ He placed five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he set the Sea on the southeast corner. ⁴⁰ Hiram finished the basins, the shovels, and the bowls. With that, all the bronze work he had been doing for King Solomon on the LORD's house was complete.

⁴¹ This is what he made: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of lattice netting to cover the two bowls; ⁴² four hundred pomegranates for the two lattice nets — two rows of pomegranates for each net covering the bowl-shaped capitals; ⁴³ the ten stands with their ten basins; ⁴⁴ the one great Sea with the twelve oxen beneath it; ⁴⁵ and the pots, shovels, and bowls. All these objects that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of burnished bronze.

⁴⁶ The king had them cast in the clay ground of the Jordan Valley, between Succoth and Zarethan. ⁴⁷ Solomon did not have all these vessels weighed, because there were so many — the total weight of the bronze was never determined. ⁴⁸ Solomon also made all the furnishings that belonged inside the LORD's house: the golden altar; the golden table for the bread of the Presence; ⁴⁹ the pure gold lampstands — five on the right and five on the left, in front of the inner sanctuary — with their gold flowers, lamps, and tongs; ⁵⁰ the gold bowls, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, incense dishes, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner sanctuary and for the doors of the main hall of the temple.

⁵¹ When all the work King Solomon had done for the house of the LORD was finished, he brought in the silver and gold and all the sacred objects that his father David had dedicated, and placed them in the treasuries of the LORD's house.

[Chapter 8] ¹ Then Solomon summoned the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, and the leaders of the ancestral families — all the chiefs of the Israelites — to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, which is Zion. ² They all gathered around King Solomon at the festival in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim. ³ When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests lifted the ark ⁴ and carried it up, along with the tent of meeting and all the sacred vessels that were in it. The priests and Levites carried everything up together. ⁵ King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel were gathered before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted.

⁶ The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD into the inner sanctuary — the Most Holy Place — and set it beneath the wings of the cherubim. ⁷ The cherubim spread their wings over the ark, sheltering it and its poles from above. ⁸ The poles extended outward and their ends could be seen from the Holy Place just in front of the inner sanctuary, though they could not be seen from outside. They are still there to this day. ⁹ There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made his covenant with Israel after bringing them out of Egypt. ¹⁰ When the priests withdrew from the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD —

¹¹ so thick that the priests could not continue to minister, because the glory of the LORD had filled his house. ¹² Then Solomon spoke: "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness. ¹³ I have indeed built you a magnificent house, a place for you to live forever." ¹⁴ Then the king turned to face the congregation of Israel, who were all standing there, and he blessed them. ¹⁵ "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel," he said, "who with his own mouth made a promise to my father David and with his own hand has fulfilled it."

¹⁶ "From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city from any of the tribes of Israel in which to build a house where my name would be — but I chose David to rule over my people Israel. ¹⁷ It was in my father David's heart to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel. ¹⁸ But the LORD said to David, 'You had the intention — and it was good that you had it. ¹⁹ Nevertheless, it is not you who will build the house; it is your son, born of your own body, who will build the house for my name.' ²⁰ The LORD has kept the promise he made. I have succeeded my father David and now sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised. And I have built this house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel."

²¹ "I have also provided a place there for the ark, which holds the covenant the LORD made with our ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt." ²² Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven. ²³ He prayed: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below — you who keep your covenant of love with your servants who walk faithfully before you with all their heart. ²⁴ You have kept your promise to your servant, my father David. You spoke it with your own mouth and fulfilled it with your own hand, as it is today. ²⁵ Now LORD, God of Israel, keep for my father David the promise you made to him: 'You will never fail to have a successor sitting before me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants walk faithfully in my ways as you have walked.'"

²⁶ "Now, God of Israel, let your word — the word you spoke to your servant David my father — be confirmed. ²⁷ But will God really live on earth? Even the heavens, the highest heavens, cannot contain you — how much less this house I have built! ²⁸ Even so, hear the prayer of your servant and his plea for mercy, LORD my God. Listen to the cry and the prayer that your servant is praying before you today. ²⁹ May your eyes be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which you said, 'My name shall be there,' so that you will hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place. ³⁰ Hear the prayer of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and when you hear — forgive."

³¹ "When someone wrongs their neighbor and is required to take an oath, and they come to swear before your altar in this house — ³² then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: declare the guilty person guilty and bring their actions back on their own head, and declare the innocent person innocent. ³³ When your people Israel are defeated before their enemies because they have sinned against you, and when they turn back to you and acknowledge your name and pray and plead with you in this house — ³⁴ then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors. ³⁵ When the sky is shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and when they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you have disciplined them —"

³⁶ "— then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave them as an inheritance. ³⁷ When there is famine or plague in the land — drought, blight, locusts, or grasshoppers — or when enemies besiege their towns, or when any disaster or sickness strikes — ³⁸ then when any of your people Israel pray and spread out their hands toward this house, each one aware of their own affliction and suffering — ³⁹ hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive them, and deal with each according to their deeds, for you know their hearts — you alone know every human heart. ⁴⁰ So they will stand in reverence before you all the days of their lives in the land you gave our ancestors."

⁴¹ "As for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of your name — ⁴² for they will hear of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray toward this house, ⁴³ then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and grant whatever they ask. Do this so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your own people Israel do — and so that they may know that this house I have built bears your name. ⁴⁴ When your people go out to battle against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD toward this city you have chosen and toward this house I have built for your name — ⁴⁵ then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause."

⁴⁶ "When they sin against you — for there is no one who does not sin — and you grow angry with them and give them over to their enemies, who carry them off as captives to a land far or near; ⁴⁷ yet if they come to their senses in the land of their captivity and repent and plead with you there, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly'; ⁴⁸ and if they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their enemies who captured them, and pray to you toward their land — the land you gave their ancestors — toward this city you have chosen and toward this house I have built for your name: ⁴⁹ then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, their prayer and their plea. Uphold their cause. ⁵⁰ Forgive your people who have sinned against you and all the offenses they have committed against you. Move their captors to show them compassion —"

⁵¹ "— for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of that iron furnace. ⁵² May your eyes be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, and may you hear them whenever they cry out to you. ⁵³ For you singled them out from all the peoples of the earth to be your own inheritance — just as you declared through your servant Moses when you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, LORD God." ⁵⁴ When Solomon finished making this entire prayer and plea to the LORD, he rose from before the altar, where he had been kneeling with his hands stretched out toward heaven. ⁵⁵ He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice:

⁵⁶ "Praise be to the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises he gave through his servant Moses. ⁵⁷ May the LORD our God be with us, as he was with our ancestors. May he never leave us or abandon us. ⁵⁸ May he turn our hearts toward him, to walk in all his ways and to keep the commands, decrees, and laws he gave our ancestors. ⁵⁹ And may these words I have prayed before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that he upholds the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel according to each day's need — ⁶⁰ so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God and there is no other."

⁶¹ "And may your hearts be fully committed to the LORD our God, to walk in his decrees and obey his commands, as you are doing today." ⁶² Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD. ⁶³ Solomon offered as a fellowship offering to the LORD twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep and goats. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD. ⁶⁴ That same day the king consecrated the middle area of the courtyard in front of the LORD's house and offered there the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold them all. ⁶⁵ Solomon held the festival at that time, and all Israel with him — a vast assembly stretching from the entrance of Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt — before the LORD our God, for fourteen days.

⁶⁶ On the fifteenth day he sent the people home. They blessed the king and left for their homes, joyful and glad, grateful for all the goodness the LORD had shown to his servant David and to his people Israel.

[Chapter 9] ¹ After Solomon had finished building the LORD's house and the royal palace — everything he had desired to do — ² the LORD appeared to him a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon. ³ The LORD said: "I have heard the prayer and the plea you made before me. I have consecrated this house you built by putting my name there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there. ⁴ As for you, if you walk before me faithfully with integrity of heart, as David your father did, and do all I command and obey my decrees and laws — ⁵ then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised David your father when I said, 'You will never fail to have a successor on the throne of Israel.'"

⁶ "But if you or your children turn away from me and do not obey the commands and decrees I have given you, and instead go and serve other gods and worship them — ⁷ then I will cut off Israel from the land I have given them. I will reject this house I have consecrated for my name, and Israel will become a byword and a mockery among all peoples. ⁸ This house will become a ruin — everyone who passes by will be appalled and will scoff, asking, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and this house?' ⁹ And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt, and they embraced other gods, worshipping and serving them — that is why the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'" ¹⁰ At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built both buildings — the LORD's house and the royal palace —

¹¹ King Solomon gave twenty towns in the region of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with all the cedar and juniper and gold he wanted. ¹² But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased. ¹³ "What kind of towns are these you've given me, my friend?" he said — and he called that region Cabul, the name it still bears. ¹⁴ Hiram had sent the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold. ¹⁵ This is the account of the labor force King Solomon conscripted to build the LORD's house, his own palace, the terraces, the wall of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

¹⁶ Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked Gezer and captured it, burning it to the ground and killing its Canaanite inhabitants. They served as his soldiers, officials, officers, commanders, and as captains of his chariots and cavalry. ²³ Five hundred and fifty officials supervised Solomon's projects and directed the workers who carried out the work. ²⁴ After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, Solomon constructed the terraces. ²⁵ Three times a year Solomon sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, along with incense offerings before the LORD. And with that, the temple was complete.

²⁶ King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion Geber, near Elath on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom. ²⁷ Hiram sent his own experienced sailors to serve in the fleet alongside Solomon's men. ²⁸ They sailed to Ophir and brought back four hundred and twenty talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.

[Chapter 10] ¹ The queen of Sheba heard reports of Solomon's fame, and came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions. ² She arrived with a great caravan — camels loaded with spices, vast quantities of gold, and precious stones — and when she came to Solomon, she spoke with him about everything that was on her mind. ³ Solomon answered all her questions. Nothing was too difficult for him; there was nothing he could not explain. ⁴ When the queen of Sheba saw all of Solomon's wisdom, and the palace he had built, ⁵ and the food at his table, the seating of his officials, the service of his attendants, their fine clothing, his cupbearers, and the steps by which he went up to the LORD's house — she was overwhelmed and left breathless.

⁶ She said to the king, "Everything I heard in my own country about your achievements and your wisdom is true. ⁷ I didn't believe it until I came and saw it with my own eyes — and even then, the half was not told me. Your wisdom and prosperity far exceed anything I heard. ⁸ How blessed are your people! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you always and hear your wisdom! ⁹ Praise be to the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and placed you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD's eternal love for Israel, he has made you king to maintain justice and righteousness." ¹⁰ Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, along with a huge quantity of spices and precious stones. Never again did such an abundance of spices arrive as what the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

¹¹ Hiram's fleet, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought great cargoes of almug wood and precious stones. ¹² The king used the almug wood to make supports for the LORD's house and for the royal palace, and to make harps and lyres for the musicians. No almug wood like it has ever been seen since. ¹³ King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she asked for, besides what he gave her from his royal generosity. Then she and her attendants returned to her own country. ¹⁴ The weight of gold that Solomon received each year was six hundred and sixty-six talents, ¹⁵ not counting what came from the revenues of merchants and traders, from all the kings of Arabia, and from the governors of the land.

¹⁶ King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold — six hundred shekels of gold for each one. ¹⁷ He also made three hundred smaller shields of hammered gold, each containing three minas of gold, and he put them all in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon. ¹⁸ The king also made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with the finest gold. ¹⁹ The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each armrest. ²⁰ And twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at each end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any other kingdom.

²¹ All of King Solomon's drinking goblets were gold, and all the furnishings of the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Once every three years it came in, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks. ²³ King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom. ²⁴ The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart. ²⁵ Year after year, every visitor brought a gift — objects of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.

²⁶ Solomon accumulated chariots and horses. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and kept with him in Jerusalem. ²⁷ The king made silver as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as common as the sycamore trees in the foothills. ²⁸ Solomon also imported horses from Egypt and from Kue — the royal merchants purchased them from Kue at the prevailing price. ²⁹ A chariot from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver and a horse a hundred and fifty. They exported them at these prices to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

[Chapter 11] ¹ King Solomon loved many foreign women. In addition to Pharaoh's daughter, he married women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites — ² nations about which the LORD had told Israel, "You must not intermarry with them, and they must not marry you, because they will surely turn your heart after their gods." Yet Solomon held fast to these women in love. ³ He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines — and his wives turned his heart away. ⁴ When Solomon was old, his wives led his heart after other gods, and his heart was no longer fully devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David's heart had been. ⁵ He followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Molek, the detestable god of the Ammonites.

⁶ Solomon did what was evil in the LORD's sight and did not follow the LORD wholeheartedly, as his father David had done. ⁷ On the hill east of Jerusalem he built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of Moab, and for Molek, the detestable god of the Ammonites. ⁸ He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods. ⁹ The LORD was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice ¹⁰ and had specifically warned him about worshipping other gods — but Solomon had not obeyed.

¹¹ So the LORD said to Solomon: "Since this is how you have behaved — since you have not kept my covenant and my decrees, which I commanded you — I will certainly tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your servants. ¹² Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime. I will tear it from your son's hand. ¹³ Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away. For the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen, I will give your son one tribe." ¹⁴ Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, who was of the royal line of Edom. ¹⁵ Earlier, when David was fighting in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.
